w10_T4_010172: A runner completed 200 kilometers during training. The distance was divided equally into 5 legs. Each leg tripled in value for time calculation. The time was multiplied by 7 (for effort units). Then by 8 (for intensity). Finally, 45 minutes were added to the total. When converted to hours (unit change from minutes to hours), how long was the total training duration?
w10_T4_010175: A shop had 117 items initially. The inventory multiplied by 8 (for packaging). Then by 5 more (for bulk orders). Then 26 items arrived. Another 63 items came in. Finally, 55 items were added. When measured in 5-unit bundles (unit conversion), how many bundles did the shop have?
w10_T4_010176: A warehouse started with 153 items. In the morning, 70 items were added. By afternoon, 26 more arrived. By evening, 194 items were shipped out. Finally, 33 more were removed. His associate at another warehouse had 95 items. How many items remained?
w10_T4_010181: A small donation box started with 32 dollars. In the morning, 73 dollars were collected. By noon, 61 dollars were added. By afternoon, 52 dollars arrived. By evening, 206 dollars was distributed to charity. How much (measured in half-dollar units as a unit conversion) remained?
w10_T4_010182: A factory had 76 units at opening. They added 52 units from production. The count multiplied by 9 (for shipment batches). By midday, it multiplied by 6 more. Then 26 units were added. Finally, the total multiplied by 9 and was converted to dozens (unit change). How many dozens were there?
w10_T4_010192: An investment account had 182 dollars. In the morning, 69 dollars were added. The total multiplied by 6 (for growth factor). Then 9 dollars in interest arrived. By afternoon, it multiplied by 4. By evening, 3767 dollars was withdrawn. His friend had 150 dollars in a separate account. How much remained in the account?
w10_T4_010194: A warehouse had 137 units. In the morning, 50 units were removed. The remaining multiplied by 8. By midday, it doubled. By afternoon, 614 units were lost. By evening, 234 more were gone. Finally, 44 units were recovered. How many units (measured as half units in a double-unit system) remained?
w10_T4_010202: A production line had 176 units starting. In the morning, this tripled. By midday, it tripled again. By afternoon, it tripled once more. Then 12059 units were removed. By evening, the remaining tripled for final count. His co-worker had 95 units. How many final units were produced?
w10_T4_010205: A student had 153 dollars initially. In the morning, they earned 73 dollars. By afternoon, 210 dollars were spent. By evening, 6 dollars more was removed. Their remaining doubled in value. Finally, 65 dollars was added. Their friend James had 85 dollars separately. How many dollars did the student have finally?
w10_T4_010209: A production capacity started at 220 units. It multiplied by 6 (for first shift). By midshift, it multiplied by 9 more. At lunch break, the total was divided by 3. After lunch, it multiplied by 3. By end of day, everything multiplied by 6. A nearby factory had 180 units (not included). How many units was the production capacity in 3-unit groupings (unit conversion)?
w10_T4_010213: A student had 57 tasks in the morning. During the morning study session, 10 more were added. By noon, 54 tasks were completed. By afternoon, the remaining tripled. By evening, 47 more were assigned. A distractor: another student had 85 tasks. How many tasks were assigned in total (measured in nines for grouping)?
w10_T4_010220: A builder started with 27 items in the morning. By mid-morning, this quadrupled. By noon, it multiplied by 8 more. By afternoon, it multiplied by 6 again. By evening, 30 items were added. The final count was converted to dozens (unit change from single items to groups of 12). How many items were in the final configuration?
w10_T4_010221: A library collection started at 123 books. In the morning, 73 were added. By noon, 22 more arrived. By afternoon, 32 books were removed. By evening, 4 books were recovered. Finally, 93 were sent to storage. A distractor: another library had 110 books. How many books remained in the collection?
w10_T4_010224: A team had 110 players in the morning. By mid-morning, 4 were removed. The team count multiplied by 4. By afternoon, 82 players left temporarily. The remaining was divided in half. By evening, 68 more joined. A partner team had 95 players (separate count). How many total players did the team have (measured in half-size units)?
w10_T4_010227: A bank account had 66 dollars initially. In the morning, 27 dollars were added. By noon, 31 dollars were withdrawn. By afternoon, 11 dollars were recovered. By evening, 66 dollars were deposited. How much was in the account at the end of the day?
w10_T4_010232: A project had 122 tasks. In the morning, 17 tasks were added. By noon, 75 more were added. By afternoon, the workload tripled. By late afternoon, it multiplied by 8. By evening, it multiplied by 5 more. A distractor: a related project had 95 tasks. When converted to hours of work (unit change), how many units total?
w10_T4_010234: A class had 135 students in the morning. They were divided into thirds (35 students per group originally, but calculation uses /3). By late morning, 71 students were added. By noon, 43 students left. By afternoon, 64 more departed. By evening, the remaining multiplied by 8. His friend managed 110 students (separate). A distractor: another school had 85 students. How many students were in the final count?
w10_T4_010235: A storage facility had 240 units. In the morning, it was divided equally into 4 sections. Then 48 units were added. By afternoon, 73 more arrived. By evening, 31 units were removed. When measured in 4-unit cases (a half measurement), how many was the final count?
w10_T4_010238: A project budget was 218 dollars. In the morning, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 1474 dollars was spent. Then 69 dollars in refunds arrived. The amount multiplied by 7 again. By evening, 58 dollars was added. A distractor: another budget was 150 dollars. When measured in 7-dollar units (unit conversion), what was the total?
w10_T4_010240: A resource pool started at 63 units. In the morning, 52 units were used. Then 6 more were removed. By noon, 75 units were added. The total was divided by 5 (into 5 equal groups). Then divided by 2 (further subdividing). Finally, 6 units were deducted. His partner had 95 units. A distractor: another pool had 85 units. How many units remained?
w10_T4_010243: A production order had 84 units. In the morning, this multiplied by 7. Then 14 units were added. By afternoon, 155 units were removed. The remaining quadrupled. By evening, it quadrupled again. How many (measured in 4-unit batches as a double system) were in the final order?
w10_T4_010248: A task list had 44 items. In the morning, it tripled. By noon, 31 items were completed. By afternoon, 35 items were added. By evening, 8 more arrived. The final list was divided in half by priority. A distractor: another list had 75 items. How many items (in terms of half-size units—when converted to half-lists) were in the main list?
w10_T4_010258: A delivery had 219 packages in the morning. By mid-morning, 27 more arrived. By noon, 33 were added. By afternoon, the count multiplied by 8. By late afternoon, 8 more were received. The total was divided into 5 equal routes. By evening, 48 packages were added to the final count. A distractor: another delivery had 95 packages. How many packages were delivered?
w10_T4_010260: An account had 169 dollars initially. In the morning, 43 dollars were added. By noon, the total multiplied by 5. By afternoon, it was divided by 5 (undoing the multiplication). Then 191 dollars were spent. By evening, 19 more was removed. A distractor: his brother had 85 dollars in a separate account. How much was left (comparing both accounts in the narrative)?
w10_T4_010270: A company had 90 employees in the morning. By mid-morning, the count quadrupled. By late morning, 70 more were hired. By afternoon, this doubled. By evening, everything doubled again. Their rival company had 150 employees (separate count). How many total employees did the company have by end of day?
